title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Spaghetti with bacon or sausage, golden crushed garlic and a smooth egg, Parmesan and black-pepper sauce.
imageAlt: Spaghetti carbonara with browned bacon or sausage, golden garlic, Parmesan and black pepper on a white plate.
personalNote: If the sauce looks a tiny bit scrambled, don’t worry. It will still taste just as good. The dish is not ruined, so don’t spiral.
equipment: Mixing bowl and fork or whisk
advancePrep: If using sausage, air-fry it until fully cooked according to its packet instructions, then chop it before you begin.
importantNotes: This feeds the two of us. Save the pasta water before you drain anything, and turn the heat off before the egg sauce goes in. The times are estimates; air-fry any sausage before starting.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: Peel and crush the cloves; do not chop them.

ingredients.name: Bacon lardons
ingredients.note: Or use a suitable sausage, already air-fried until fully cooked and chopped.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: For heavily salting the pasta water.

ingredients.name: Reserved pasta water for the wok
ingredients.note: Save this before draining the pasta.

ingredients.name: Extra reserved pasta water
ingredients.note: Save this too: 500 ml in total for the original two-serving batch. Use only as needed to loosen the sauce.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: Hen eggs suitable for lightly cooked dishes.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.note: Coarsely crushed, or use pepper powder.

steps.title: Get the garlic and water ready
steps.description: Peel the garlic and crush the cloves—don’t chop them for this one. Boil two kettles of water, one after the other if you’re using the same kettle. Pour them into a big saucepan, bring it to the boil and salt it heavily.
steps.heat: High heat to boil the water

steps.title: Cook the spaghetti and save the water
steps.description: Boil the spaghetti until al dente. It’s usually about 8 minutes, but check the packet and give a strand a taste. Before you drain it, save both measured amounts of pasta water in a jug. Then drain the spaghetti and leave it aside.
ingredients: Reserved pasta water for the wok
steps.doneness: Tender spaghetti with a little bite.
steps.tip: The 8-minute timer is a first check. Follow the packet if it gives a different time. Al dente means cooked but still slightly firm in the centre.

steps.title: Mix the egg sauce
steps.description: Beat the eggs, grated Parmesan and black pepper together in a bowl. That’s the sauce. Have it ready before the pasta goes back into the wok.

steps.title: Cook the bacon or prepared sausage
steps.description: Heat the wok on medium and add the bacon lardons, or the sausage you’ve already air-fried until cooked and chopped up. Give it about 5 minutes, until it starts releasing some oil.
steps.doneness: Fat is collecting in the wok.

steps.title: Add the crushed garlic
steps.description: Add the crushed garlic and squish it around for another 3 minutes, until it goes golden. Keep an eye on it so it doesn’t burn.
steps.warning: Check that the bacon is fully cooked before continuing; do not rely on the timer alone.

steps.title: Toss the pasta in the wok
steps.description: Add the pasta water measured for the wok and get it boiling vigorously. Put the spaghetti in and toss it around until most of the water is absorbed. Taste it now and make sure it’s cooked how we like it.
ingredients: Reserved pasta water for the wok
steps.doneness: Pasta cooked to your liking; most of the water absorbed.

steps.title: Turn off the heat and add the sauce
steps.description: Turn the heat OFF before the sauce goes in. Add the egg mixture and immediately start squishing and tossing the pasta around vigorously, so the sauce goes smooth instead of the eggs scrambling.
steps.doneness: A smooth sauce coating the spaghetti.
steps.tip: Keep the pasta moving as soon as the egg sauce goes in.
steps.warning: Make sure the hob is off before adding the egg sauce.

steps.title: Loosen the sauce and serve
steps.description: If it looks too dry, add a little of the extra pasta water and mix again. Add a bit at a time until it loosens up, then serve straight away. If the sauce looks a tiny bit scrambled, don’t worry: it still tastes just as good. The dish is not ruined, so don’t spiral.
steps.tip: If the sauce looks a tiny bit scrambled, don’t worry. The dish is not ruined, so don’t spiral.

substitutions.title: Sausage instead of bacon
substitutions.text: Use a suitable sausage that has already been air-fried until fully cooked, then chopped. Follow its packet for cooking time and temperature.

substitutions.title: Black pepper
substitutions.text: Coarsely crushed pepper or pepper powder both work.

troubleshooting.title: Sauce too dry?
troubleshooting.text: Add a little of the extra reserved pasta water and stir. Keep adding it in small amounts until the sauce loosens.

troubleshooting.title: A few scrambled bits?
troubleshooting.text: Don’t worry: it will still taste just as good. The dish is not ruined, so don’t spiral.

storage: Best eaten straight away. If you have leftovers, cool and refrigerate them within 1–2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. A splash of water helps loosen it, although the egg sauce may firm up.
foodSafety: Cook the bacon or sausage fully. For the lightly cooked egg sauce, use British Lion or Laid in Britain hen eggs, or pasteurised egg. Serve immediately.
servingSuggestion: Serve immediately, while the sauce is loose and smooth.
